name: Sea Sirine
body:
SEA SIRINE
CR 6

This appears to be a beautiful woman with glistening eellike skin ranging in shades from silvery green to crimson.

XP 2,400
CN(E) Medium magical beast (aquatic)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +15

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 16, flat-footed 15 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural)
hp 57 (9d10+9)
Fort +8; Ref +12; Will +7
Immune mind-affecting effects

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 60 ft.
Melee 2 talons +12 (1d6), bite +7 (1d4 plus poison)
Special Attacks bardic performance, sirine’s song, sneak attack +3d6
Spell Like Abilities (CL 8th):

3/day—cause fear (DC 16), charm person (DC 16), deep slumber (DC 18), shout (DC 19)

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 18, Con 12, Int 14, Wis 19, Cha 21
Base Atk +9; CMB +9; CMD 22
Feats Dodge, Flyby Attack, Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Finesse
Skills Fly +7, Knowledge (history) +10, Perception +15, Perform (sing) +13, Stealth +14
Languages Auran, Common
SQ kiss of the deeps, short flight

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bardic Performance (Su)

A sirine may use bardic performance as a 4th-level bard (9 rounds/day), and can use countersong, distraction, fascinate, inspire competence, and inspire courage. Levels in the bard class stack with this ability.

Kiss of the Deeps (Su)

The kiss of the sea sirine grants water breathing to the recipient as the spell of the same name (CL 9th).

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 15; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d3 Con; cure 1 save.

Short Flight (Ex)

Sea Sirines are akin to flying fish in their ability to swim forcefully through the water and then launch themselves from the waves to fly a short distance. If they use a full-round action to run while swimming at or near the water’s surface, on their next turn they can launch themselves into the air and fly (speed 50 feet, maneuverability average) for up to 2 rounds. At the end of this time they fall back into the sea (or whatever surface is below) and if more than 10 feet high risk taking falling damage. While flying they are able to use their Flyby Attack on foes.

Sirine Song (Su)

When a sirine sings, all non-sirines within a 300-foot spread must succeed on a DC 20 Will save or become enthralled (see below). The effect depends on the type of song the sirine chooses, and continues for as long as the sirine sings and for 1 round thereafter. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by any of that sirine’s songs for 1 hour. These are sonic, mindaffecting effects. The save DC is Charisma-based. Enthralled creatures behave in one of the following four ways, which the sirine chooses when she begins singing.

Captivation: This functions exactly like a harpy’s captivating song.

Fascination: Affected creatures are fascinated.

Obsession: An obsessed victim becomes defensive of the sirine and does all he can to prevent harm from coming to her, going so far as attacking his allies in her defense. The victim is not controlled by the sirine, but views her as a cherished ally. This is a charm effect.

Slumber: The victim immediately falls asleep, rendering the creature helpless. While the sirine is singing, no noise will wake the sleeping creature, though slapping or wounding him does. The creature continues sleeping for 1d4 minutes after the sirine stops singing, but can be awakened by loud noises or any other normal method.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate or warm water
Organization solitary or school (2–7)
Treasure standard

Sea Sirines are a race of beings akin to harpies. These creatures are known to dwell on craggy reefs, atolls, and the lagoons of volcanic atolls. Sea sirines appear as beautiful women with soft iridescent eel-like skin and long slender fins protruding from their shoulder blades in the manner of a flying fish. Considered a bane to sailors, regions that they are known to dwell in are largely avoided by fisherman and pirate alike.

Like their aerial relatives, sea sirines need human males in order to breed, and the result of this union is always a clutch of eggs which hatch into sea sirines who are then adopted into the school. The male partner is most often slain.
